subject: Q4 OKR synthesis + incident impact (final scores & narrative)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Q4 OKR synthesis + incident impact (final scores & narrative)

Team — quick one. We need a concise final scoring and a 2–3 paragraph narrative for the exec QBR that explains the numbers, with a focus on the production incident in Oct that materially affected Platform Reliability and Developer Velocity. Targets and asks below: 

- Please provide final numeric scores for the following OKRs (0–100 scale): Platform Reliability, Developer Productivity, Serving Cost per Token, Customer Expansion (top 5 accounts).
- For each objective, include one sentence rationale and one short remediation/next-step.
- Add a short incident impact paragraph that states (a) minutes of impact, (b) primary customer-facing symptoms, (c) mitigations we applied, and (d) how we’ll change guardrails/process.

Attachments: I attached the working spreadsheet with my preliminary numbers. Please update directly and ping when done. Need final copy by EOD Friday (2026-11-06) so we can fold into the QBR packet.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Product & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

[attachment: q4-okr-scores-draft.xlsx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Q4 OKR synthesis + incident impact (final scores & narrative)

Rishi — uploaded my scores and a short rationale. Key points below; spreadsheet updated (see tab "Scores_LB").

Platform Reliability: 45
- Rationale: Incident on 2026-10-21 led to ~55 minutes of partial service degradation for hosted API in us-west-2; SLOs breached for 2 customers during peak. We cannot claim the previously planned 75+ score.
- Next step: Add automated cross-region failover in our canary path and accelerate the hotfix to kernel selection logic.

Developer Productivity: 70
- Rationale: Internal infra rollouts went smoothly; SDK adoption improved. The incident slowed a few deploys but not the overall cadence.
- Next step: Add postmortem action items to the dev oncall checklist.

Serving Cost per Token: 62
- Rationale: Quantization and batching initiatives reduced unit cost, but incident-related reroutes increased short-term egress/replication cost.
- Next step: Finalize quantization rollout and add cost guardrails for reroutes.

Customer Expansion (top 5 accounts): 78
- Rationale: Strong pipeline and two closed proofs, but renewal conversations with Acme were delayed by the incident.
- Next step: Executive outreach and a technical remediation package for impacted accounts.

Incident impact paragraph (for narrative):
- On 2026-10-21 at ~09:20 UTC, a kernel selection regression caused elevated p99 latencies and partial request failures for the hosted API in us-west-2. Total visible customer impact ~55 minutes; internal mitigation included immediate traffic routing to us-west-1 and the emergency rollback. We’ve opened a postmortem and will ship the kernel fix + automated cross-region failover by mid-Q1.

Attachment: q4-okr-scores-draft.xlsx (tab: Scores_LB)

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-06T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Q4 OKR synthesis + incident impact (final scores & narrative)

Thanks Laura — I reviewed and made a couple of edits in the doc attached (incident-timeline.pdf) and in the narrative draft. Two notes: 

1) Platform Reliability score: propose lowering to 40 (vs 45) to reflect the downstream SLA credits we gave and the multi-customer impact documented in the incident timeline. For the QBR, a conservative score + transparent remediation resonates better with execs.

2) Executive narrative: I drafted a two-paragraph blurb that: (a) states the score and ties it directly to the incident, (b) summarizes what customers saw and what we fixed, and (c) lists the three remediation commitments with owners (SRE: cross-region failover, Runtime: kernel fix, Product: customer remediation packs).

On Oct 21 I coordinated with Acme SRE and oncall; John, we appreciated your timely response. Laura, please pull Vivek's paragraph into the final doc and make the language QBR-ready.

Thanks all — this is great. Final decisions and how we'll present them in the QBR: 

- Final scores (locked): Platform Reliability 40; Developer Productivity 70; Serving Cost per Token 62; Customer Expansion (Top 5) 78. Spreadsheet tab: "Final_Scores_RM".
- Executive narrative (2 paragraphs) consolidated and attached (q4-exec-narrative-final.docx). Vivek's language adopted verbatim for the incident paragraph; Laura's remediation bullets preserved as owner/action lines.
- Acme/External ask: John, I added a one-paragraph, non-technical summary for customer-facing slides and pasted a version below; feel free to edit: "On Oct 21, a temporary software regression caused elevated latencies and partial request failures for a subset of users. We routed traffic, rolled back the change, and restored service within one hour. We will add automated cross-region failover and ship a kernel selection fix in Q1 to prevent recurrence."

Open actions before QBR packet final: 
1) Laura — copy final narrative into the QBR deck (slide 4) and add the scorecard table.
2) Vivek — confirm owners and shipment dates for the three remediation commitments in the action slide.
3) PMM (cc'd separately) — draft the external slide language for customer execs; coordinate with John for tone.

I updated HubSpot with the interim note (see https://hubspot.company/deal/ACME-7890) and uploaded the final doc to Drive (https://drive.company/shared/q4-okr-narrative-draft). I’ll circulate the final deck by Monday morning.

Thanks — Rishi
